question: What's new this week in Agentic AI hiring trends and in tooling/frameworks worth knowing about?

what_to_study.summary: Recent arXiv papers (Nov 17‑23 2026) introduce new resources: TOUMAII tool‑calling preference dataset, ChatAtom open‑source multi‑agent system for molecular‑dynamics simulation, AstronautBench benchmark for agent self‑improvement, plus safety, calibration, and budget‑aware orchestration studies.

what_to_share_with_learners.summary: Agentic AI positions surged to 48,025 on Indeed, making up 71% of AI job postings, a 55% YoY increase in AI‑skill ads and a 297% decade‑long rise in “agentic” terminology, indicating a dominant hiring focus on agentic technologies.
what_to_share_with_learners.source_note: Indeed; Agentic AI Jobs Index; Stanford AI Index; SoftwareFinder

digest.linkedin_post_draft: 🚀 Agentic AI hiring is exploding! In the past week Indeed listed 48,025 open Agentic AI positions—the highest weekly total ever recorded. The curated Agentic AI Jobs Index shows 71 % of all AI‑related roles now focus on agentic technologies, up from about 55 % a year ago. Stanford’s AI Index reports a 55 % YoY rise in AI‑skill ads and a 297 % decade‑long increase for the term “agentic.” Companies are racing to staff teams that can orchestrate LLMs with external tools, embed RL‑from‑human‑feedback loops, and build safe multi‑agent pipelines. If you have hands‑on experience in LLM orchestration, prompt‑ops, or agent safety, now is the time to showcase those skills. Bottom line: Agentic AI is no longer a niche research area – it’s the dominant hiring focus across the AI job market.

training_module_ideas.learning_objective: Learners will be able to design and implement an LLM‑driven agent that autonomously calls external tools and evaluate it using the TOUMAII dataset.
key_points: Overview of tool‑calling architectures (e.g., LangChain, ReAct)
Hands‑on use of the TOUMAII dataset for prompting and evaluation
Building a production‑grade pipeline that integrates APIs (calendar, database, code execution)
Strategies to showcase orchestration projects on a résumé

training_module_ideas.topic: Safety Guardrails & RLHF for Autonomous Agents
training_module_ideas.learning_objective: Learners will be able to construct safety verification checks and a basic RLHF loop for an autonomous agent, aligning with current hiring emphasis on safety and alignment.
key_points: Understanding safety‑focused hiring patterns from Stanford AI Index and SoftwareFinder
Designing reward models and safety checklists for agents
Implementing a simple RLHF loop for tool‑using agents
Preparing interview‑ready artifacts that demonstrate safety expertise

training_module_ideas.topic: Evaluating & Improving Agentic Systems with Benchmarks
training_module_ideas.learning_objective: Learners will be able to run the AstronautBench benchmark on a multi‑agent system and interpret self‑improvement metrics to guide development.
key_points: Introduction to AstronautBench and its evaluation criteria
Setting up the ChatAtom multi‑agent framework for a scientific workflow
Running benchmark episodes and analyzing performance gains
Formulating improvement strategies and communicating results in job interviews
training_module_ideas.based_on: AstronautBench benchmark (early) and hiring demand for multi‑agent coordination (strong)
